### The Ascent

</div>

Every workshop begins the same way: cluttered, half-finished, smelling faintly of wax that hasn't set yet. Mine is no different. I'm **Avlokita** — a Computer Science student who spends most days somewhere between *this compiles* and *why does this compile*, slowly assembling a pair of wings I didn't inherit.

I'm learning Software Engineering the way Icarus learned altitude — not from a manual, but from actually going up and paying close attention to what the air does to feathers. Every stack I pick up, every framework I break and rebuild, is one more feather bound on a little more carefully than the last.

I fly toward **AI**, because it's the closest thing we have to teaching a machine to reach. I fly toward **Full-Stack Development**, because I'd rather build the sky I'm testing than borrow someone else's. I fly toward **Open Source**, because nobody reaches real altitude alone — you climb faster in formation, alongside people who understand exactly what you're risking. And I fly toward **Game Development**, because it's the most honest place to study flight: worlds built specifically so failure is safe, and trying again is the whole point.

I'm still climbing. Every project is a higher thermal. Every late night spent chasing one stubborn bug is, in its own small way, a rehearsal for altitudes I haven't earned yet. The goal was never to avoid the fall — it's to contribute something real to this field, find the others out there building their own wings, and keep climbing toward whatever greatness in this craft actually turns out to mean.
